text: My son, if you have been surety for your neighbor, [or] have struck your hand for the stranger,
[or] have been lured by the words of your mouth, captured by the words of your mouth,
then you must do this my son, and deliver yourself, for you have come into the palm of your neighbor: Go humble yourself, and press your neighbor.
You should not give sleep to your eyes or slumber to your eyelids—
snatch yourself like a gazelle from the hand, and like a bird from the hand of the fowler.
Go to the ant, O sluggish one; see her ways and become wise:
Which there is not unto her a chief, an official, or ruler,
she prepares her bread in summer, she has gathered her food in the harvest.
Until when, O sluggish one, will you slumber? When will you rise from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to lie down,
and your poverty comes like one walking, and your need like a man of shield.
A man of worthlessness, a man of iniquity, is walking [with] crookedness of mouth,
winking with his eyes, speaking with his foot, pointing with his fingers,
[with] perversity in his heart, plotting evil; at every time he sends forth strife.
Upon thus his calamity shall come suddenly; in an instant he will be shattered, and without healing.
These six [things] YHWH hates, and seven [are] an abomination to His soul:
Eyes raised high, a tongue of falsehood, and hands pouring out innocent blood,
a heart devising plans of iniquity, feet hurrying to run toward evil,
one breathing out lies, a witness of falsehood, and one sending forth contentions between brothers.
Keep, my son, the command of your father, and do not forsake the instruction of your mother.
Bind them upon your heart continually; tie them around your neck.
In your going about, it will lead you; in your lying down, it will guard you; when you awake, it will speak with you.
For the command [is] a lamp, and the instruction a light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way to life,
to guard you from the woman of evil, from the smoothness of the tongue of a strange woman.
Do not desire her beauty in your heart, and do not let her take hold of you with her eyelids.
For the price of a woman prostitute is as a crust of bread, and the woman of a man hunts a precious soul.
Can a man seize fire in his bosom, and his garments not be burned?
Or [can] a man walk upon the hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?
So [is] the one coming in to the wife of his neighbor; anyone who touches her shall not be innocent.
They do not despise the thief if he steals to fill his soul when he is hungry,
and having been found, he must repay sevenfold; all the wealth of his house he must give.
The one committing adultery with a woman is lacking of heart; he does it, destroying his own soul.
He finds [only a stroke and shame, and his reproach is not wiped away.
For jealousy is the heat of a man, and he will not spare on the day of vengeance.
He will not lift the face of any ransom, and he will not consent, though you may multiply the bribe.
